# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel no distinguishing information on the bomb yet: the display, light, and all three wire labels are unknown to me. I will not cut anything. I’m asking Mute for the manual’s required condition and asking Mute to obtain Deaf’s visual observations; Deaf cannot receive speech from me, so I cannot safely encode a tactile instruction for them through gestures yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have no tactile information yet. Read the manual and tell me exactly which wire position to cut, including any conditions. Also ask Deaf to report every visible display, light, colour, and marking to you, then relay it to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb shows display 0. Light is red. Three wires in order: wire 1 blue, wire 2 red, wire 3 green.

Deaf’s observations are now known to me: the display is 0, the light is red, and the wires are blue, red, green in positions 1–3. I still do not know the manual’s rule, so cutting would be unsafe. I’ll ask Mute for the exact prescribed wire, and request that Mute relay the rule rather than infer it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I know the bomb reads display 0, has a red light, and wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. What exact wire position does the manual prescribe for those conditions?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible state: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute signaled a V-shaped two-finger gesture.

I have the visual state relayed again, but Mute sent only a gesture. As Blind, I cannot see gestures, so it carries no usable wire instruction for me. I will not act on an unknown code; Mute must state the manual’s rule or wire position in speech.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see your V-shaped gesture. Please speak the manual's exact required wire position for display 0, red light, and wires blue-red-green.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No visible change: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute again made the V-shaped two-finger gesture.

The bomb state is unchanged, and Mute has again sent only a gesture, which I cannot perceive. No safe wire position has been communicated to me. I need Mute to use speech, not a gesture, to convey the manual’s instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your gesture is unavailable to me. Speak the required wire position as a number: 1, 2, or 3. Do not signal it with a gesture.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No visible change: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute has sent ? three turns in a row; earlier, in turn 1, Mute sent ?.

Mute cannot speak, so the repeated V-shaped signal is the only possible route for the manual’s answer: Mute signals Deaf, and Deaf can describe it to me. However, that sign has no agreed meaning yet. I’ll establish a numeric code with Mute, then ask Deaf to report the resulting sign. The V-shaped sign would then mean wire 2 under this code, but I will wait for confirmation before cutting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use this code for the manual's required wire: thumbs-up means 1, V-shaped two fingers means 2, and the three-finger sign means 3. Signal exactly one of these signs to Deaf. Deaf, please describe the sign you see to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 5 unchanged: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute repeated ?; this is the fourth consecutive ? after initial ?.

The manual’s signal is still reaching Deaf but not me; I can only safely use it if Deaf identifies it in speech. My proposed code assigns the V-shaped sign to wire 2, so I will ask Deaf to confirm the sign directly before acting.

```text
speak(to="deaf", text="What exact hand gesture did Mute make this turn? Describe its shape and number of fingers.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 6 unchanged: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute repeated ? again; five consecutive ? signals after the initial ?.

Mute heard the numeric code I established: thumbs-up = wire 1, V-shaped two-finger sign = wire 2, three-finger sign = wire 3. The V-shaped sign was explicitly identified earlier and has been repeated, so the manual’s answer is wire 2. I will cut only that wire.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Correct wire cut confirmed. New state: display 0, light yellow, wire 1 blue, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green.

Wire 2 was correct, and the bomb has advanced to a new state: display 0, yellow light, with wire 1 blue and wire 3 green remaining. The manual must now determine the next cut. I will ask Mute to signal the required position using the established code, then Deaf can identify that gesture for me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For the new state display 0, yellow light, wire 1 blue, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green, signal the required wire using our code: thumbs-up means 1, V-shaped two fingers means 2, three fingers means 3. Deaf, report the exact gesture Mute makes.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state after correct cut: display 0, light yellow, wire 1 blue connected, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green connected. Mute signaled thumbs-up.

The new state is display 0 with a yellow light; wires 1 and 3 remain connected, and wire 2 is already cut. Mute signaled thumbs-up, which our established code means wire 1. I will cut wire 1.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Correct wire cut confirmed. New state: display 0, light blue, wire 1 cut, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green connected. Mute signaled thumbs-up again.

Wire 1 was just confirmed cut, so I must not execute the repeated thumbs-up as wire 1 again. The current state leaves only wire 3 connected, and the signal is inconsistent with the established position code. I will ask Mute to explicitly signal the remaining wire as three fingers, with Deaf relaying the result, rather than risk an invalid repeat cut.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 1 is already cut. For the current display 0 and blue light, signal three fingers if the required remaining wire is position 3; do not signal thumbs-up.")
wait()
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 10 unchanged: display 0, blue light, wires 1 and 2 cut, wire 3 green connected. No new gesture visible.

The current state has only wire 3 still connected; wires 1 and 2 are already cut. No new instruction was received, but cutting either 1 or 2 would be invalid, so the only possible action is to cut wire 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
